sources.title: İlyas Kemaloğlu, Sibir Hanlığı, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi (2019)
sources.note: Political outline, population groups, livelihoods, imports and living Siberian Tatar communities. Article gives 1493 for Ibak death whereas edited 1494 correspondence survives; public text uses 1490s. No demographic totals adopted.

sources.title: S. F. Tataurov and F. S. Tataurov, Archaeological collections from Isker (2016), pp. 77 to 85
sources.note: Direct Russian full text. Museum collections, loss of context, chest keys, bone tools and imports. English initials and some abstract terms are mistranslated; Russian body used. Same-work DOI 10.20874/2071-0437-2016-33-2-077-085.

sources.title: S. F. Tataurov, Archaeological sites of Siberian khanates: markers of statehood (2017), pp. 352 to 362
sources.note: Direct Russian PDF. Regional pottery, symbolic arrows and seal rings; interpretations are attributed rather than treated as direct proof of unified administration. DOI 10.22378/2313-6197.2017-5-2.352-362.

sources.title: A. A. Adamov, Kuchum settlement: capital city or historical myth? (2021)
sources.note: Direct original Russian scholarly abstract, Golden Horde Review 9(2), pp. 359 to 373, DOI 10.22378/2313-6197.2021-9-2.359-373. Explicitly challenges temporary-headquarters interpretation using fortifications, crafts and thick cultural deposits.

sources.title: A. A. Adamov, Earlier material from Isker (2020)
sources.note: Russian abstract directly/indexed verified. Russian венчики means vessel rims and пряслице spindle whorl; English abstract misleadingly calls them rings and distaff. DOI 10.30853/mns200582.

sources.title: History and culture of Turkic peoples through sources: three studies of Sibir (Kurgan, 2011)
sources.note: Entire volume conservatively grouped as one work. Matveev/Tataurov administrative study printed pp. 33 to 37, atalyks p. 35; Rakhimzyanov diplomatic study pp. 78 to 80, 1597 quote p. 79; Ryabinina foreign policy study pp. 90 to 95, remedies p. 94. PDF indices are printed pages minus one. Full text directly checked; screenshots fail. The quote is a Russian textual witness, not verified original Turkic script.

sources.title: Little-known documents on the history of the Siberian Khanate: edited diplomatic records
sources.note: Direct complete scholarly document transcription. Sections II.1 to 2 explicitly distinguish Tatar-written letter from Russian translation; section III.6 captive-family list dated 4 September 1598. Royal testimony represents Muscovite officials, not neutral population evidence.

proposedOverrides.name: Khanate of Sibir
proposedOverrides.summary: A western Siberian khanate of shifting river, forest and steppe connections.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact imported 1492 to 1600, three nearly identical polygons. No aliases: broad siberians is a culture record; Kazan/Golden Horde/Russian Empire/Russia distinct. Historical antecedents precede 1492; conquest extends across 1582 to 1598 and later resistance. Atlas fixed outline cannot show Kuchum expansion or fragmented tributary authority. Isker permanent-capital debate presented with 2016/2021 alternatives. No precise population total or unsupported toilet system. Russian translated writing explicitly labeled; no fabricated Arabic-script reconstruction. TDV 1493 death of Ibak conflicts with edited 1494 correspondence, so 1490s used. Sources count the entire 2011 proceedings volume together.
